title: Hosted API latency shock and streaming interruption synthesis
content:
Summary:
On 2026-11-10 from ~17:21:00 UTC to ~17:39:00 UTC we observed a P0 latency and partial availability degradation for the Hosted API (generation + streaming). Customer-facing symptoms: elevated request tail latencies, increased streaming reconnects, and a ~10-15% spike in 5xx responses for affected routes. Root cause was a compounding interaction between a recently rolled-out locality-aware multiplexing routing policy, transient edge DNS resolution thrash in two EU regions, and an autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration for the mux worker pool.

Severity and impact:
- Severity: P0 (customer-impacting, widespread)
- Incident window: ~17:21:00 - 17:39:00 UTC (18 minutes of sustained elevated errors/latency; sporadic elevated tail latency persisted up to 17:50 as caches warmed)
- Affected regions: eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 primarily; some cross-region fallthrough increased load in us-east-1
- Customer-visible metrics at peak: p50 ~340ms (baseline ~210ms), p95 jumped from ~480ms to ~3.2s, p99 ~9.4s; 5xx rate for streaming/generation routes rose to 12% (baseline <0.5%)
- Internal impact: increased request queue length on mux workers, KV-cache miss amplification, higher network connect latencies, surge of recovered connections on edge gateways

Detection timeline (concise):
- 17:19:40 UTC: Synthetic monitors for streaming window p95 begin to show divergence.
- 17:21:03 UTC: Pager triggered (SRE alert: HOSTEDAPI-P95-THRESHOLD) for sustained p95>2s in eu-west-1.
- 17:22:00 UTC: Oncall first-response team begins triage. Initial dashboards show 5xx increase and connection churn metrics on edge proxies.
- 17:24:10 UTC: Spike correlated with rollout of routing policy 'mux-locality-v2' (canary fraction 10%) — new per-region multiplexing logic deployed 17:15 UTC.
- 17:26:40 UTC: DNS error spikes observed on edge (increased NXDOMAIN/timeout for certain service endpoints) in eu regions; RTT to upstream DNS increased.
- 17:27:20 UTC: Autoscaler for mux-worker pool shows cooldown preventing additional replicas (cooldown configured 6m, recent scale-in happened at 17:21).
- 17:29:05 UTC: Immediate mitigations applied: canary routing policy rolled back, mux-worker pool manually scaled to target, edge DNS cache TTLs adjusted and CDN edge reconfiguration pushed.
- 17:36:50 UTC: Error rates and tail latency begin to decline; p95 back under 1s by 17:40 and near-baseline by 17:50 after cache warm and connection stabilization.

Root cause analysis (post-triage):
This incident was a classic multi-factor failure where independent small issues interacted to create customer-visible outages. Key contributing factors: 
1) Canary routing policy 'mux-locality-v2' introduced changes to connection lifecycle handling that increased short-lived connection churn under transient DNS failures. The canary route altered fallback ordering and attempted additional upstream connections when an edge returned a DNS timeout, which amplified concurrent connection attempts.
2) Edge DNS subsystem experienced transient resolution timeouts and elevated RTTs in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. The DNS thrash appears to have been caused by an external resolver upstream encountering a brief overload combined with an aggressive negative-caching TTL configuration we recently landed (reduced TTL for NX responses).
3) Mux-worker autoscaler had a cooldown and scale-in policy that allowed the pool to be undersized during the early stages of the incident. Because a scale-in completed at ~17:21, the autoscaler refused to scale up for ~6 minutes despite queued requests and increasing processing latencies.
4) Lack of a targeted synthetic that exercises combined routing+edge-dns failure modes meant the canary's behavioral regression wasn't caught before rollout.

Sequence that led to outage:
- New routing canary (10% traffic) changes connection fallback behavior -> when an upstream DNS lookup timed out, the routing code retried or opened extra connections -> connection churn increases load on mux workers and edge proxies -> autoscaler is in cooldown and cannot react quickly -> request queues grow -> upstream request timeouts convert to 5xx and tail latency balloons -> as more traffic is retried, problem amplifies until mitigations applied.

Immediate mitigations executed (timeline & owners):
- 17:29:05 UTC: Roll back 'mux-locality-v2' canary to previous stable routing policy (owner: Marcelo Rivera).
- 17:29:20 UTC: Manually scale mux-worker pool +20% (owner: Priya Anand).
- 17:30:10 UTC: Push edge DNS TTL adjustments and flush selected resolver caches at CDN edge (owner: Lucas Nguyen).
- 17:31:00 UTC: Activate fallback-only routing for streaming-heavy routes for affected customer segments until metrics normalized (owner: Aisha Kapoor).
- 17:36:50 UTC: Begin step-down mitigations and monitoring for regression (team: eng-sre).

Why the rollback + manual scale fixed it:
Removing the routing change stopped the extra connection attempts pattern; scaling mux workers absorbed the queued work; fixing DNS cache behavior reduced transient DNS errors so retried lookups weren't necessary. The combination returned system to a steady state faster than any single mitigation alone.

Monitoring and detection gaps identified:
- Missing synthetic for the combined failure mode: we have unit/integration tests for routing changes and synthetic DNS checks, but no end-to-end synthetic that exercises routing behavior under DNS timeouts.
- Alert thresholds triggered on p95, but not on early connection churn signals (connection attempt rate, connection resets per second) with sufficient sensitivity.
- Autoscaler configuration doesn't include a 'sustained queue length' override to bypass cooldown during sudden queue growth.

Runbook gaps and recommended runbook changes:
- Add a subsection to the Hosted API rollout/runbook: pre-rollout combined failure synthetic (routing + DNS failure simulation) for any mux/routing changes.
- Add quick rollback checklist entry specific to routing policy canaries, including immediate manual scale and edge DNS validation steps.
- Add an autoscaler emergency override command (k8s HPA override + SRE CLI) with documented IAM restrictions so oncall can force scale outside cooldown windows.
- Create an 'edge-dns-thrash playbook' that documents safe cache TTL adjustments and the specific CDN edge commands we executed during this incident.

Longer-term corrective actions (owners and target dates):
- Fix mux connection lifecycle logic to avoid creating extra redundant connections on DNS timeouts (eng-serving-runtime, owner: Mateo Silva, target: 2026-12-05).
- Rework autoscaler logic to include a queue-based scale trigger and reduced cooldown for mux-worker HPA (eng-platform-engineering, owner: Priya Anand, target: 2026-11-24).
- Add combined-routing+dns synthetic tests to CI and production synthetic fleet, including canary gating that fails safe on regressions (devexp + eng-sre, owner: Marcelo Rivera, target: 2026-11-30).
- Postmortem follow-up engineering ticket to harden edge resolver selection and patch negative-caching TTL policy (edge-infra team, owner: Lucas Nguyen, target: 2026-11-18).

Communication and customer notes:
- Slack incident channel created at 17:22 UTC (#incident-hostedapi-2026-11-10). Engineering updates provided every 6–8 minutes during mitigation window.
- Post-incident a short customer-facing note will be drafted by CS (owner: Riya Patel) and routed to impacted account contacts with a summary of impact and planned mitigations.

Action items (concrete and assignable):
1) Create SRE-4129: Implement autoscaler queue-trigger + emergency override (assignee: Priya Anand) due 2026-11-24.
2) Create SRE-4130: Add combined routing+DNS synthetic to production synthetic fleet and CI gating (assignee: Marcelo Rivera) due 2026-11-30.
3) Code PR: fix mux connection retry behavior on DNS timeouts (assignee: Mateo Silva) due 2026-12-05.
4) Edge infra ticket: review negative-caching TTL policy and identify safe defaults (assignee: Lucas Nguyen) due 2026-11-18.
5) Runbook update: routing-canary quick rollback checklist + how-to scale mux workers (owner: Aisha Kapoor) due 2026-11-14.
6) Customer comms draft for impacted customers (owner: Riya Patel) due 2026-11-13.

Lessons learned (brief):
- Small behavior changes can amplify under transient infra faults; canaries must be exercised under realistic failure modes before rollout.
- Autoscalers and scale-in cooldowns can be a single point of friction that prevents rapid recovery; we need queue-driven scale triggers and an emergency bypass.
- Monitoring should include early signs (connection churn, DNS error spikes) with automated correlation to recent rollouts.

Appendix (quick reference):
- Key dashboards: Hosted API p95/p99 by region, connection attempts/reset rate, mux-worker queue length, edge DNS error rate.
- Primary linked artifacts: JIRA SRE-4129, GitHub PR #2291 (routing canary), internal logs bucket 'internal://logs/2026-11-10-hostedapi-latency-wave'.
- Contact list for follow-up: Aisha Kapoor (oncall lead), Marcelo Rivera (routing), Priya Anand (autoscaler), Lucas Nguyen (edge infra), Mateo Silva (runtime).

If there are additional logs or traces needed for the RCA, call them out in the #incident-hostedapi-2026-11-10 channel and tag owners. This doc is intended as the synthesis to feed a final postmortem and runbook updates.
